rows.grounds: describing the lord as independent and infinite

items.question: How does the all-pervading Lord preside over the five instruments?
premises: The all-pervading Lord, whose body is space, always presides by that power.
He presides over the group of five instruments.
He is unsupported, made of lordship, and endless.
items.inference: The independent, space-bodied Lord eternally governs the five instruments through his own power.
uncertainties: The exact referent of tayā is inferred from the preceding context as Śiva's power or prior agency.
items.plain_english: The all-pervading Lord, whose body is space, always presides by that power over the five instruments; he is unsupported, lordly, and endless.

items.question: How does the Lord set the pervasive principle into motion?
premises: The Lord impels the pervasive one by his own power.
Māyā, whose form is action, is situated as the instrument.
Below Māyā is the coiled power.
items.inference: The Lord uses Māyā as his instrument to impel the pervasive principle, with the coiled power situated below Māyā.
uncertainties: The identity of vyāpinaṃ is not explicit in this verse and may refer to a pervasive tattva or principle from context.
items.plain_english: He impels the pervasive one by his own power, using Māyā, whose form is action, as the instrument; below Māyā lies the coiled power.

items.question: What range of manifestation is described as arising in the teaching?
premises: The world arises as effect beginning with sound and point.
This range extends up to Sadāśiva.
This range also begins with earth in the teaching.
items.inference: The teaching presents a continuous manifestation from earth up to Sadāśiva, arising through stages such as sound and point.
uncertainties: The compound structure of kāryamityādijagadudbhavaḥ allows slight variation in parsing, but the overall meaning is clear.
items.plain_english: In the teaching, the world arises as effect beginning with sound and point, extending from earth up to Sadāśiva.

rows.grounds: what was taught to the speaker

items.question: What has been declared about that range and what topic follows next?
premises: All that range is declared to be derived from primal nature.
It is joined with destruction and arising.
The measure of all worlds, as told by the speaker's teachers, will now be explained.
items.inference: The mutable manifested range is classified as prākṛta, and the text now turns to the measure of all worlds taught by the gurus.
uncertainties: The scope of prākṛta here may be technical and broader or narrower than ordinary usage.
items.plain_english: All that is declared to be derived from primal nature and subject to arising and destruction; now the measure of all the worlds, as taught to me by my own teachers, will be explained.

items.question: Why will the measure of the worlds be told briefly and what begins the list?
premises: That measure will be told briefly so the mind may quickly pass through it.
The enumeration begins within the cosmic egg.
The first named figures include Ananta, Kāla, Kūṣmāṇḍa and Hāṭaka, and Brahmā and Hari.
items.inference: A concise account is given to aid rapid mental traversal of the worlds, starting with Ananta and other figures within the egg.
uncertainties: The exact cosmological placement of each named figure depends on the wider compendium context.
items.plain_english: That will be explained briefly so that the mind may quickly pass through it: within the egg are Ananta, Kāla, Kūṣmāṇḍa and Hāṭaka, and Brahmā and Hari.

rows.grounds: count of worlds in that level
the seven tattvas in which worlds are distributed

items.question: How many worlds belong to outer Nivṛtti and across which tattvas are they distributed?
premises: There are a hundred Rudras together with their heroes.
Outer Nivṛtti has one hundred and eight worlds.
These are distributed each in turn across the seven tattvas: water, fire, wind, space, ego, intellect, and root nature.
items.inference: The outer Nivṛtti level comprises 108 worlds apportioned across the seven lower tattvas from water up to prakṛti.
uncertainties: The relation of the hundred Rudras to the 108 worlds is compactly stated and may rely on the surrounding cosmological scheme.
items.plain_english: There are a hundred Rudras with their heroes, and outer Nivṛtti has one hundred and eight worlds, distributed one by one across the seven tattvas of water, fire, wind, space, ego, intellect, and primal nature.
